rowText: The AI models screen closes instead of doing anything: A on almost any control shuts it. Found on the Deck 2026-09-21, blocked the whole screen and meant the filters feature shipped 2026-09-20 had never once been usable.

setup.screen: Ollama tab, Manage AI models, opened with the filters panel already showing
setup.note: The panel state and the filter choices were read before anything was pressed, and put back at the end.

steps.action: A on the Manage AI models button
A on the filter row 'Open source only (recommended)'
steps.result: PASS - the choice changed from off to on and the screen stayed open. Before tonight this press closed the whole screen.

steps.action: A on the same row again
steps.result: no change - see the finding below

steps.action: Down, then A on 'Also try open-weight models'
steps.result: PASS - the original choice is selected again, screen open

steps.action: Up twice to the Filters button, A
steps.result: PASS - screen open, ring stayed on Filters
PASS - the filter panel closed (ten rows down to none), screen still open, ring still on Filters
panel reopened, leaving the screen as it was found

verdictSentence: Six A presses on the models screen, on three different controls, and the screen never closed once. Before tonight the first press on any of them closed it.

alsoFound.what: The three licence rows -- 'Open source only', 'Also try open-weight models', 'Any installed model' -- are one three-way choice, not three independent switches. Pressing A on a row selects it; pressing A on the same row again does NOT turn it back off. To undo, move to the row you had before and press A there.
alsoFound.whyItMatters: Anyone restoring settings after a check will get it wrong if they assume pressing A twice undoes it. Measured here: the first press moved the choice from 'Also try open-weight' to 'Open source only', and a second press on the same row left it there.
alsoFound.isItABug: No. That is how a choice of one out of three should behave. Written down because it is not obvious from the screen and it caught this run.

notCovered: A on a model's tick box -- the catalog list showed no rows with the current filters, so no tick box was on screen to press
B while typing a model name by hand -- needs the on-screen keyboard
Ticking the first model in a fresh list, which needs a catalog row
The try-order picker writing settings on an unchanged Done
